artboards.title: 7 · Mobile setup, Two players, rules shown
1 · Game setup, Two players, rules shown

annotations.text:
Dot states
• Small gray dot: not clickable
• Blue ring: valid start (MV-2, MV-4)
• Solid dot in the current player's color: selected Dot1
• Dashed ring in the current player's color: valid Dot2 neighbor (MV-3, MV-5)

Board shown at N=4, 48 px squares. Sample players: Оля and Богдан on Ukrainian screens, Ann and Bob on English ones.

Languages: the UA / EN toggle is at the top right of every screen. Ukrainian is the default (I18N-2, I18N-3); screen 15 shows English.
All text comes from src/i18n/locales.
Spec: docs/dot-line-game/requirements.md

Mobile layout (below 640 px wide)
• Board on top, centered; panel below at full width (MB-2)
• Squares stay 48 px while the board fits, then shrink to fit the screen, 24 px minimum (MB-3)
• Each dot is tappable across a whole square, up to 44 px (MB-4)
• Buttons are at least 44 px tall (MB-8)
• Rules: toggle at the bottom; shown by default on setup, hidden during a game (RL-2, RL-3)
• Languages: UA / EN toggle at the top right, 44 × 44 px buttons, Ukrainian by default; screen 14 shows English (I18N-2, I18N-3, I18N-5)

From 640 px up, the desktop layout on the Desktop page applies.
Open for confirmation: 640 px breakpoint, board-first order, shrink instead of scroll.

Versus computer mode (spec: docs/computer-opponent/spec.md, issue #6)
• Game mode switch at the top of setup: Versus computer (default) | Two players (CM-1, CM-2, CM-6)
• Difficulty switch Easy | Normal, only in Versus computer, Normal by default (CM-5..7)
• Versus computer: the person enters name, color and size; the Opponent fieldset is read-only: robot + Computer with its automatic color (CM-4, CM-9)
• Robot icon: Material Symbols smart_toy as inline SVG, currentColor, aria-hidden (CM-13, CM-37)
• Computer's turn: robot + Computer in Turn, pulsing "Thinking…" in place of the hint, every dot idle (board locked), Stop still works (CM-14, CM-16, CM-17)
• Person's turn: "Your turn"; the computer's last line keeps a 4 px halo in its color until the person draws (CM-18, CM-19)
• Result: "You won!" or robot + "Computer won", winner first in the scores (CM-27)
• Sample person: Ярослава Петрук / Alexandra Brown, 15 characters, never cut; names wrap when space runs out (GS-1, GB-5)
• New text uses the proposed message keys listed in design.md
